To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ERCC1 expression in human papilomavirus-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinomas is associated with prognosis in patients who received surgery and adjuvantradiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy.

we have identified a novel method to assess ERCC1 protein in SCCHN tumors and found that low ERCC1 expression correlates with longer survival in patients with HPV-negative tumors treated with surgery and CRT.
the excision repair cross complementing group 1 protein expression in head and neck cancer is associated with patient outcomes and can be quantified using the AQUA method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of molecular markers that can be used to predict the outcome of patients with SCCHN treated by surgery and adjuvants.

the development and evaluation of a new method for quantitative assessment of protein expression in tissue microarrays (TMAs) using automated quantitative analysis (Aqua) of immunohistochemical staining.
the identification of biomarkers that can predict treatment outcome in patients with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the head and the neck.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ERCC1 expression level is an independent prognostic marker of survival in patients with HPV-negative head and neck cancer treated by surgery and adjuvent radiotherapy.
ERCC1 protein levels are not a good predictor of response to cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy in patients with head and neck cancer.
ERCC1 expression is a prognostic marker for patients treated with surgery ± RT/CRT, but not for patients treated with RT/CRT alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a difference in survival among patients whose tumors express high or low ERCC1 protein, as determined using the HPA02973 antibody.
ERCC1 expression in HPV-negative SCCHN is a biomarker for cisplatin and radiotherapy resistance and a predictor of survival in patients treated with surgery ± adjuvant radio/chemoradiotherapy.
ERCC1 expression is associated with cisplatinum sensitivity and radioresistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ERCC1 expression in SCCHN is associated with patient survival and that this is dependent on whether or not adjuvant RT is administered.
we can use ERCC1 expression as a prognostic factor in HPV-negative SCCHN patients treated with surgery, radiotherapy, and CRT.
we can identify a subgroup of head and neck cancer patients who have tumors that express low levels of the DNA repair protein ERCC1.
